trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Mysuru, MC No.876/2019
case_name: Sri M R Naveen Chandra vs Smt Pooja S Padmini
facts_of_case: The petitioner-husband filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ia) & (ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty. The trial court dismissed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: Parties can settle disputes through compromise and the court will give effect to such settlements.
legal_principles.held: The parties have arrived at an amicable settlement of the dispute and accordingly they have filed a compromise petition under Order XXIII Rule 3 of Civil Procedure Code, 1908.
applicable_acts_sections: Civil Procedure Code — Order XXIII Rule 3

legal_principles.principle: A compromise agreement can be a full and final settlement of disputes, precluding further claims.
legal_principles.held: The respondent/wife accepted to receive Rs.10,00,000/- towards her permanent alimony and it is final settlement amount, there will be no further claim by the respondent/wife against the appellant/husband in any manner whatsoever.

outcome.final_order: The parties arrived at an amicable settlement and the appeal was allowed with a compromise petition under Order XXIII Rule 3 of Civil Procedure Code, 1908.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
